notes.artefacts: cobblestone_wall posts without properties render as '?'

visual.summary: Well level 3: a 3 x 3 cobblestone ring with a slab lid; too small and plain, and the wall posts show as placeholder blocks.
problems: Far too small and bare for the kingdom's water source (23 to 28 blocks): build a 5 x 5 well with a raised two-course stone basin, posts, a windlass beam with a rope or chain and a proper roof.
The cobblestone wall posts have no connection properties and show as "?" placeholder blocks; use log posts instead.
The flat oak slab lid reads as a box: give it a steep gable roof with dark eaves and ridge.
Give each level its own extras (a trough and a bucket barrel at level 2, bushes, flowers and moss at level 3).

notes.levels: Adds a cauldron tub, flower pot, moss carpets and two more lanterns: visible, but mostly props rather than a new feature.
notes.roof: Same roof as L2, no overhang past the posts.

visual.summary: Level 3 adds a cauldron water tub, a flower pot on the barrel, moss carpets on the rim and extra lanterns.
problems: Ignores Carlton's note 'still not circular': the rim course at y=1 has exactly the same outline as the rejected v5 (5x5 with the four corners cut, square 3x3 pool inside); from the top it still reads as a square with notched corners.

Make the rim read as a round ring without growing past a middle size: e.g. keep the cut outer corners AND fill the inner corners of the ring at y=1 (1,1),(3,1),(1,3),(3,3) so the ring is an even-thickness octagon round a plus-shaped pool, or go to a 6x6 ring (.####. / #....# / ... / .####.) with chamfered corners; v3's 7x7 was 'too big'.
Cauldron at (0,1,4) and barrel at (4,1,0) stand in the rim's cut corners and make the top view square; move both onto the grass outside the ring.
L3's additions are mostly props: give it one clearer new feature (e.g. a trough or stone step/path to the well).
Rim height is now correct: one course (y=1) above the grass with the water flush at y=0 (groundLayer 0, noted, not a fault).
